caption: Black tax comes before rent in my head, even though it leaves my account after. Is that just how it works in your family too?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R9 500
p/m salary
Living in Giyani
slides.body:
Female, 23
Single, lives alone
Job: Till operator, local supermarket
Net salary: R9 500 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: Backroom off the main road, shares a yard tap
slides.body: It's not much, but it's mine, and nobody can raise it on a whim like the last place did.

slides.title: Black tax
slides.includes: My grandmother's groceries and my two younger siblings' school needs
slides.body: It goes before rent in my head even though it leaves after. There's no version of my budget without this line.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: My own food for the month, plus extra when I visit home
slides.body: I eat smaller than this number some weeks so the visit-home extra doesn't run out.

slides.title: Transport
slides.includes: Taxi fare to the till and back, six days a week
slides.body: The fare went up twice this year. My wage didn't.

slides.title: Airtime & data
slides.includes: Enough to check on the kids after school
slides.body: This is the one call I will never let lapse.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Stokvel, funeral policy, toiletries, a savings attempt that keeps losing
slides.body: I promised myself R500 a month into savings. It's the first thing that disappears when black tax goes up.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R9 500. That's about R30 a day, and payday at the till is the same date every month whether my family's needs are or not.

slides.title: I stopped guessing where the R9 500 went
slides.body:
I uploaded my statement to Beyond Horizon and it showed me black tax and groceries were nearly forty percent of my pay, every single month.

No bank login needed.
